title: Blondin & Tonry 2007, ApJ 666, 1024 — Determining the Type, Redshift, and Age of a Supernova Spectrum (SNID)
content: The SN type (subtype) is simply determined as the type (subtype) of the best-match template(s) for rlap greater than some cutoff value rlap_min. We usually discard correlations with rlap < 5. Last, the age of an input spectrum is determined with a typical accuracy sigma_t <= 3 days.

citations.quote: We usually discard correlations with rlap < 5
citations.used_for: snid_best_type(type_iib, few_days_past_max): SNID best-fit type = IIb at appropriate epoch. SNID determines the SN type as the type of the best-match template(s) above a reliability cutoff (rlap > 5), and determines spectral age to within ~3 days. This is the expected signature for a IIb and not for a IIP/Ib best fit. ROOT METHODOLOGY is grounded (Blondin & Tonry 2007), but no published numeric likelihood ratio P(SNID best=IIb | IIb)/P(SNID best=IIb | not) exists. Direction strongly favors IIb.
